interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. Preoperative PSA was elevated at 5.8. The surgical findings included a pathological stage of pT3a with positive surgical margins, but no extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, or lymphovascular invasion. The absence of removed lymph nodes, indicated by "no lymph nodes were removed," widens uncertainty regarding nodal status, as pNx is not equivalent to pN0. The biopsy showed a lower grade (Gleason 3+3) compared to the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3, ISUP grade group 3).

Countervailing findings include the absence of extraprostatic extension and seminal vesicle invasion. The primary uncertainty lies in the postoperative PSA trajectory and subsequent follow-up, as this information is currently missing. Information regarding postoperative PSA levels and their subsequent trend would significantly revise the prognosis. The current heuristic horizon suggests a time frame for recurrence. The fixed estimated horizon is 63.30 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 41.14–85.45 months; its coverage has not been validated.
